           BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA

         IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                       )
         OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY                         )
         FOR AN ORDER OF THE COMMISSION                            )
         APPROVING ITS NEW EXTRA LARGE LOAD                        )
         TARIFF AND TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF                        )      CASE NO. PUD2026-________
         SERVICE FOR EXTRA LARGE LOAD                              )
         CUSTOMERS AND A REGULATORY ASSET TO                       )
         RECOVER COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH                             )
         PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION SOFTWARE                           )

                                                  APPLICATION

               COMES NOW Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company, hereinafter “Applicant,” “OG&E,”
         or “Company,” and shows as follows:

            I.      APPLICANT:
                  OG&E is an investor-owned electric public utility incorporated within the State of
         Oklahoma, subject to the regulatory authority of this Commission, and has the following address
         as its principal place of business:
                                       Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company
                                       321 N. Harvey Avenue
                                       Oklahoma City, Oklahoma 73102

                  Applicant is represented in these proceedings by the below signed counsel. All
         correspondence, pleadings and communications with respect to this proceeding should be directed
         to all named counsel.

            II.     FACTS:
                1.      Pursuant to Final Order No. 753440 in Case No. PUD2025-000038, the
         Commission directed Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E” or “Company”) to file an
         application establishing a tariff applicable to large load customers no later than July 1, 2026.
                  2.     This directive coincides with the enactment of Oklahoma House Bill 2992, to be
         codified at 17 O.S. §§ 901–905, which requires electric utilities to establish and maintain separate
         tariffs, terms and conditions of service for large load customers and to ensure that such customers
         pay the costs fairly allocable to them and commit to a minimum term of service.
                3.      OG&E is experiencing increasing interest from prospective and existing customers
         whose electric demand meets or exceeds the statutory threshold for large load treatment, including
         customers with expected peak demand of 75 megawatts or greater. Existing tariffs are not designed
         with the customer protections required to address the unique risks and characteristics associated
         with customers of this magnitude, necessitating the development of a dedicated tariff framework.



                                                          1

                4.      A central concern associated with serving extra-large load customers is the risk of
        the potential for adverse impacts on other customers based on the unique characteristics of serving
        extra-large load customers. To address these potential risks, OG&E has developed the proposed
        Extra Large Power and Light (“XLPL”) Tariff and accompanying Terms and Conditions of Service
        for Extra Large Load Customers (“T&CXLLC”). Service under the XLPL Tariff requires long-
        term service agreements and the XLPL tariff and T&CXLLC incorporate a comprehensive set of
        customer protections for other customer classes.
               5.      In addition to requesting approval of the XLPL Tariff and T&CXLLC, OG&E has
        conducted a cost and benefit study of portfolio optimization modeling software in accordance with
        Final Order No. 753440. OG&E is submitting that study in this proceeding as required by the
        Order. The study provides the required cost and benefit analysis and demonstrates that such
        software can improve resource planning by identifying least-cost portfolios and evaluating system
        performance under a range of future conditions. OG&E proposes to defer the costs associated
        with implementation of this software through a regulatory asset for consideration in a future rate
        case.


            III.   LEGAL AUTHORITY:
                The Commission has jurisdiction over this Application and authority to grant the relief
        requested herein pursuant to Article IX, § 18 of the Oklahoma Constitution; 17 O.S. §§ 151 et seq.,
        including but not limited to 17 O.S. §§ 152 and 901–905; and the Oklahoma Corporation
        Commission’s Rules of Practice, OAC 165:5, and applicable rules governing electric utility
        service, including OAC 165:35.


            IV.     RELIEF REQUESTED:

                 WHEREFORE, OG&E respectfully requests that the Commission approve the Extra Large
        Power and Light Tariff, the Terms and Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers,
        and a regulatory asset to track costs associated with the implementation of portfolio optimization
        modeling software. OG&E further requests any other such relief that the Commission may deem
        fair, just, and reasonable.
